crossRefs.note: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat…
but his delight is in Yahweh’s law. On his law he meditates day and night.
Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
Blessed is the man to whom Yahweh doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit.
Blessed are those whose ways are blameless, who walk according to Yahweh’s law.
It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice, and said to him…
But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and his brothers, James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?
Then the disciples came, and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this saying?”
“Woe to the world because of occasions of stumbling! For it must be that the occasions come, but woe to that person…

parallels.note: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”

translations.web: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
translations.bsb: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”
translations.kjv: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.
translations.asv: And blessed is he, whosoever shall find no occasion of stumbling in me.
